knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4)

```{r setup}
library(bayesSampleMix)
```

## Model and algorithm

The target model is $y \sim \text{Poisson}(\exp(x'\beta))$. Contaminated units
follow Poisson($\lambda_0$) with $\lambda_0 \sim \text{Gamma}(1, 1)$ under
`M0`/`Mjoint`, or a rival Poisson regression under `M1`.

The log link has no convenient conjugate augmentation, so $\beta$ is updated by
a Metropolis–Hastings step whose proposal is the Laplace (Gaussian)
approximation to its full conditional: Newton/IRLS iterations
(`mixture_control(irls_steps = 3)`) started at the current value locate the
mode, and the proposal covariance is the inverse negative Hessian there. Once
the Newton iterations converge, the proposal does not depend on the current
state and the step is an exact independence sampler with high acceptance.
The acceptance rate is reported by `summary()`.

## Example

```{r data}
beta <- c(1.2, 0.5, -0.4)
d <- simulate_mixture_data("poisson", n_prob = 300, n_nonprob = 300,
                           contamination = 0.25, beta = beta, x_shift = 2,
                           seed = 301)
```

```{r fit}
fit <- mixture_fit(y ~ x1 + x2, d$prob, d$nonprob, family = "poisson",
                   n_iter = 1500, burnin = 500, seed = 1)
pooled <- baseline_fit(y ~ x1 + x2, rbind(d$prob, d$nonprob[names(d$prob)]),
                       family = "poisson", n_iter = 1500, burnin = 500, seed = 1)
rbind(truth = beta, naive_pooled = coef(pooled), mixture = coef(fit))
summary(fit)
```

The target coefficients are recovered, while naive pooling attenuates them.
As in the logistic case, the contamination fraction is over-estimated (true
value 0.25): the background Poisson($\lambda_0$) density also describes
many compatible units reasonably well, and the `Mjoint` covariate term
allocates some compatible units in the tails of the P covariate distribution
to the contaminating component. In 10 simulated data sets of this design the
posterior mean of $1-\pi$ averaged about 0.40 under both `M0` and `Mjoint`,
but about 0.26 under `M1`, whose rival regression matches the contaminating
mechanism used here. The error is conservative (it reduces precision, not
accuracy of the target coefficients). Contaminated units whose counts happen
to be consistent with the target model (their mean function intersects the
target mean function) cannot be identified, which limits the AUC:

```{r scores}
filter_auc(1 - d$nonprob$contaminated, filter_scores(fit))
plot(fit, type = "scores")
```

Posterior expected counts for new covariate values:

```{r predict}
predict(fit, data.frame(x1 = c(-1, 0, 1), x2 = 0))
```

## Sensitivity to the IRLS setting

The original implementation used three Newton steps. Increasing them makes the
proposal state-independent to numerical precision; on well-behaved data the
results are essentially identical:

```{r irls}
fit25 <- mixture_fit(y ~ x1 + x2, d$prob, d$nonprob, family = "poisson",
                     n_iter = 1500, burnin = 500, seed = 1,
                     control = mixture_control(irls_steps = 25))
rbind(irls_3 = coef(fit), irls_25 = coef(fit25))
c(irls_3 = fit$acceptance, irls_25 = fit25$acceptance)
```
